verdict.rationale: Fly.io's docs describe a streamlined deploy flow (fly launch) and 'hardware-isolated VMs that boot in under a second' and scale automatically with 'no rearchitecting' as you grow, positioning it as a no-server-management full-stack/edge platform (fly-io-docs-1, fly-io-docs-14, fly-io-docs-15). However, extensive community reports document concrete operational failures — stuck/unreachable machines, deploys failing 70-80% of the time, Postgres machines not spinning up, and Fly's own incident response advising users to 'run multiple instances to mitigate the impact of single-host failures' — which directly contradicts the promise of infrastructure-free operation (fly-io-comm-2, fly-io-comm-5, fly-io-comm-9, fly-io-comm-19). This is a genuine dispute: vendor claims effortless full-stack deployment with no server management, but hands-on evidence shows users must actively manage redundancy and troubleshoot infra failures. Missing for 10: a true FaaS/serverless-functions product feature (Fly Machines are VM-based, not function-triggered compute), independent benchmarks validating uptime/scaling claims, and resolution of the documented reliability issues.
